newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: AMP confirms Virgin/Bank of Scotland talks.
newsitem.headline: AMP confirms Virgin/Bank of Scotland talks.

text.p: The AMP Society confirmed on Tuesday that it was holding talks with Richard Branson's Virgin group and the Bank of Scotland about establishing a new banking operation in the United Kingdom.

AMP spokesman Bob Pritchard said the talks, reported in recent days as involving only AMP and Virgin, were based on briefings with the U.K. press which revealed a bit more than the conservative life office would have liked.
"Richard Branson apparently talked to some of the media over there and mentioned that we are in discussions regarding some developments in banking," Pritchard said.
"It is true we are in discussions with Bank of Scotland and Virgin itself as to where we might go from here but nothing has been signed," he told Reuters.

Australia's largest insurance and funds management group has made no secret of its desire to become an even larger player in the U.K. financial services market where it already operates Pearl Assurance and lost out this year in the two billion pound bidding contest for Scottish Amicable.
AMP managing George Trumbull said earlier this year that AMP could easily handle a takeover of up to A$5 billion and was looking at substantial purchases in the U.K. and United States.
It has been cited as a possible bidder for insurers Norwich Union Plc and the National Provident mutual group in U.K. press reports over the last four months but nothing has happened.
Pritchard said the talks about a new banking operation were the result of AMP's successful involvement in the Virgin Direct financial services joint venture.

AMP planned to inject a further 290 million pounds to fund the expansion of Virgin Direct, which had grown enormously since AMP joined the venture in 1995. It now had 200,000 customers and more than one billion pounds in funds under management.

Virgin Direct marketing director Tony Wood told Reuters in London on Monday the company was desperately keen to enter the banking sector and had been in talks with potential partners for some time. "We are not afraid to take on anybody," said Wood, who also told The Times newspaper that AMP would back Virgin Direct's plan to operate a 24-hour telephone banking operation.
This would seek to win high-income customers who were now served by the major clearing banks, the paper said.

The Sydney Morning Herald newspaper said on Tuesday that Bank of Scotland would run the new operation which would trade as Virgin Bank, adding to the already eclectic grouping of Virgin assets which includes an airline, the V2 music division, and railway investments.
AMP's Pritchard said the AMP which has more than A$90 billion of funds under management and plans to list sometime next year, was not necessarily interested in a bank with a large branch network.
Instead, he pointed to the attraction of technological developments in Australia "where you are looking more to a virtual bank than an actual bank".
